title: The Robin
phrases: first to any freshly dug earth

doing.t: is puffed up round as an apple
is singing its thin, silvery song
is listening with its head cocked to one side
is eyeing up a crumb of cheese
is splashing about in a saucer of water

close: Just the robin, close enough to see where the orange breast meets the grey.
Only the robin, plump as a bauble, in the middle of the page.

roles.main: for the orange-red breast and face
roles.dark: for the eye, the beak and the shadow under the wing
roles.light: for the pale belly and the catchlight in the eye
roles.accent: for the blue-grey edging around the breast

firstMark: Start with the eye: one round dot of {dark}, leaving a pinprick of paper for the shine.
Start with the curve of the breast in a light pass of {main}.

title: The Wren
phrases: a voice far bigger than the bird
tail flicked up like a thumb
barely the size of a walnut

doing.t: is belting out a song with its tail cocked
is creeping along like a mouse
is giving someone a good telling-off
is carrying a beakful of moss

close: Just the wren, tail up, close enough to see the barring on its wings.
Only the wren, a plump brown speck in a sea of white paper.

roles.main: for the russet-brown back and wings
roles.dark: for the fine barring and the eye
roles.light: for the pale stripe over the eye
roles.accent: for the pinkish legs

firstMark: Start with the cocked tail: three short strokes of {main}, pointing straight up.
Start with the eye: a single dot of {dark}, with the pale stripe above it left as bare paper.

title: The Blue Tit
phrases: upside down as often as not

doing.t: is cracking a sunflower seed held under one foot
is pulling strips off a paper seed packet
is giving its feathers a brisk shake
is pecking through the foil top of a milk bottle
is hanging upside down by its toes

close: Just the blue tit, upside down, filling the page.
Only the blue tit's face, a white mask ringed with navy.

roles.main: for the yellow breast
roles.dark: for the eye stripe, the bib and the eye
roles.light: for the white cheeks
roles.accent: for the blue cap and wings

firstMark: Start with the dark stripe through the eye in one sharp line of {dark}.
Start with the round belly in a light, even layer of {main}.

title: The Long-Tailed Tit

doing.t: is fluffed into a ball with its tail sticking out
is calling to the rest of the flock
is balancing with its tail held out straight
is gathering strands of cobweb for its nest

close: Just the long-tailed tit, a round body and a tail longer than the rest of it.
Only the long-tailed tit, with the whole length of its tail on the page.

roles.main: for the rosy pink on the shoulders and flanks
roles.dark: for the black stripe over the eye and the tail
roles.light: for the white crown and breast
roles.accent: for the red ring around the eye

firstMark: Start with the tail: one long, tapering stroke of {dark}, longer than the body.
Start with the black stripe that runs from the eye back over the head, in {dark}.

title: The Goldfinch

doing.t: is twittering a tinkling, liquid song
is flicking its wings to flash the gold
is turning its red face this way and that
is prising seeds out of a teasel head
is pulling thistledown for its nest

close: Just the goldfinch's head, close enough to see where the red meets the white.
Only the goldfinch, side on, wings shut, each colour showing.

roles.main: for the buff back and breast
roles.dark: for the black wings and the cap
roles.light: for the white cheeks and wing spots
roles.accent: for the red face and the gold wing bar

firstMark: Start with the wing: a short black block of {dark}, leaving a stripe of paper for the gold.
Start with the cap, a neat band of {dark} across the top of the head.

title: The Blackbird

doing.t: is singing a slow, fluting song
is hopping a few steps, then standing stock still
is chinking its alarm call with its tail raised
is tossing leaves aside with its beak
is pecking at a fallen apple

close: Just the blackbird's head, with its yellow eye ring and orange beak.
Only the blackbird, mid-song, beak open, on an empty page.

roles.main: for the black body
roles.dark: for the deepest shadows under the wing and tail
roles.light: for the blue sheen along the back and wings
roles.accent: for the orange beak and eye ring

firstMark: Start with the beak: a neat wedge outlined in {dark}, left empty for the orange.
Start with the head in {main}, working around a ring of bare paper for the eye.

title: The Song Thrush

doing.t: is repeating its favourite phrase with great pride
is turning to show off its speckled front
is sitting with one foot tucked up
is swallowing a rowan berry whole

close: Just the song thrush's breast, every speckle a small dark arrowhead.
Only the song thrush, standing tall, in a circle of white paper.

roles.main: for the mid-brown back and wings
roles.dark: for the speckles and the eye
roles.light: for the cream breast
roles.accent: for the buff wash on the flanks

firstMark: Start with the speckles: a scatter of small arrowheads in {dark}, largest at the bottom.
Start with the eye, a round dot of {dark}, then the brown cap above it in {main}.

title: The Kingfisher

doing.t: is sitting perfectly still with its beak pointed down
is bobbing its head up and down
is shaking droplets from its feathers
is whizzing past like a blue spark

close: Just the kingfisher's head and long beak, as large as the page allows.
Only the kingfisher, side on, with the orange and the blue meeting cleanly.

roles.main: for the turquoise back and crown
roles.dark: for the long beak and the eye
roles.light: for the white throat and neck patch
roles.accent: for the coral-red feet

firstMark: Start with the long beak: two straight lines of {dark} meeting in a point.
Start with the band of {main} across the top of the head.

title: The Grey Heron
phrases: a grey coat and a yellow dagger
lifts off like a folding chair

doing.t: is standing motionless on one leg
is hunched up with its neck sunk into its shoulders
is stalking forward one careful step at a time
is peering down its beak with a frown
is flapping away with its legs trailing behind

close: Just the heron on one leg, tall and thin down the middle of the page.
Only the heron's head and neck, with a beak like a letter opener.

roles.main: for the grey back and wings
roles.dark: for the black crest and the stripe down the neck
roles.light: for the white neck and face
roles.accent: for the yellow beak and eye

firstMark: Start with the black plume behind the eye: one long, thin flick of {dark}.
Start with the curve of the folded wing in a light layer of {main}.

title: The Barn Owl
phrases: honey and pepper on the back

doing.t: is staring ahead with dark, unblinking eyes
is tilting its whole face to one side to listen
is preening the speckled feathers of its chest
is gliding low with its face tilted down
is hanging in the air on wide, pale wings

close: Just the barn owl's face, a white heart with two dark eyes.
Only the barn owl, wings wide, floating across the page.

roles.main: for the honey-coloured back and wings
roles.dark: for the eyes and the fine speckles
roles.light: for the white face and underparts
roles.accent: for the pale grey dappling on the wings

firstMark: Start with the two eyes: round dots of {dark}, set wide apart, with a thin ring of paper around each.
Start with the outline of the heart-shaped face in a faint line of {main}.

title: The Tawny Owl

doing.t: is turning its head almost all the way round
is hooting a long, wavering hoo-hoo-hoo
is blinking one eye very slowly
is sleeping upright with its eyes shut tight
is stretching itself tall and slim to hide

close: Just the tawny owl's face, with its two dark eyes and the pale V between them.
Only the tawny owl, round and streaky, sitting in the centre of the page.

roles.main: for the warm chestnut feathers
roles.dark: for the eyes and the dark streaks
roles.light: for the pale eyebrows and the spots on the wings
roles.accent: for the yellowish beak

firstMark: Start with the eyes: two big, solid circles of {dark}, leaving a speck of paper in each.
Start with the pale disc of the face, edged with a ring of {main}.

title: The Puffin
phrases: a beak like a striped sweet

doing.t: is waddling about on bright orange feet
is tapping beaks with its mate
is looking extremely solemn
is carrying a beakful of grass for its burrow
is whirring past on frantic wings

close: Just the puffin's head, close enough to see the dark triangle above each eye.
Only the puffin, standing upright, black and white like a dinner jacket.

roles.main: for the black back and collar
roles.dark: for the deepest shadows and the eye
roles.light: for the white face and front
roles.accent: for the orange beak and feet

firstMark: Start with the beak: a triangle outlined in {dark}, with the stripes to fill in later.
Start with the black collar across the chest in {main}.

title: The Cygnet

doing.t: is stretching one stubby grey wing
is asleep with its head tucked under a wing
is peeping for its mother
is nibbling at a strand of weed
is riding on its mother's back

close: Just the cygnet, a grey pear shape with a dark beak.
Only the cygnet, round and downy, with plenty of white page around it.

roles.main: for the grey down
roles.dark: for the beak and the eye
roles.light: for the pale fluff on the breast
roles.accent: for the faint buff tinge on the back

firstMark: Start with the beak: a short wedge of {dark}, with the eye just above it.
Start with the round body in a light, scribbly layer of {main}.

title: The Mallard Ducklings

doing.t: are piled together in a heap
are tumbling along after one another
are all looking the same way at once
are paddling along in single file
are dabbling with their tails in the air

close: Just the three ducklings in a row, each one facing a different way.
Only one of the ducklings, close up, with every wisp of down.

roles.main: for the yellow down on the faces and bellies
roles.dark: for the brown backs and the stripe through each eye
roles.light: for the fluffy edges and the shine in the eyes
roles.accent: for the small beaks and webbed feet

firstMark: Start with the eye stripes: one short dash of {dark} through each eye.
Start with three overlapping ovals of {main}, drawn very lightly.

title: The Swallow
phrases: a chin the colour of brick

doing.t: is twittering away to itself
is running its beak along its tail streamers
is sitting with its wingtips crossed behind it
is swooping low with its tail spread
is carrying a pellet of mud
is feeding a row of open-beaked chicks

close: Just the swallow, wings swept back, tail streamers long and fine.
Only the swallow, side on, with its red chin and navy back.

roles.main: for the glossy navy back and wings
roles.dark: for the eye and the deepest blue of the wingtips
roles.light: for the creamy belly
roles.accent: for the brick-red chin and forehead

firstMark: Start with the forked tail: two long, thin strokes of {main}, like an open pair of scissors.
Start with the red chin, then edge it with a narrow band of {dark}.

title: The Great Spotted Woodpecker

doing.t: is chiselling at a peanut
is calling out a sharp, single tchik
is peering round to show the red patch on its nape
is drumming so fast its head is a blur
is hopping upwards in short jerks

close: Just the woodpecker, side on, so the black, white and red all show.
Only the woodpecker's head, with the red patch at the back of it.

roles.main: for the black back and wings
roles.dark: for the eye, the moustache stripe and the beak
roles.light: for the white shoulder patches and face
roles.accent: for the scarlet under the tail and on the nape

firstMark: Start with the white shoulder patch: outline it in {dark} and leave the inside as bare paper.
Start with the black moustache stripe across the cheek in a firm line of {main}.

title: The Bumblebee
phrases: too round to fly, and yet

doing.t: is cleaning its face with its front legs
is buzzing crossly at nothing in particular
is resting with its wings folded flat
is bumbling from flower to flower
is buried head first in a foxglove

close: Just the bumblebee, close enough to see every stripe of fuzz.
Only the bumblebee, side on, legs dangling, filling the page.

roles.main: for the yellow bands
roles.dark: for the black body and legs
roles.light: for the white tail and the shine on the wings
roles.accent: for the orange pollen on the legs

firstMark: Start with the fuzz: short strokes of {dark} flicked outwards from the middle of the body.
Start with the yellow band behind the head in {main}, using small circles for the fluff.

title: The Ladybird

doing.t: is opening its red wing cases to fly
is keeping still in the hope of being ignored
is tucking its wings back under its spotted shell
is climbing to the very tip of a grass stalk
is snoozing in a cluster with dozens of others

close: Just the ladybird, drawn as big as a plum, spots and all.
Only the ladybird from above, a red dome with seven black spots.

roles.main: for the glossy red wing cases
roles.dark: for the spots, the head and the legs
roles.light: for the white marks on the head and the shine on the shell
roles.accent: for the warm orange where the red thins at the edges

firstMark: Start with the seven spots in solid {dark}, before any red goes down.
Start with the shine: leave a small oval of bare paper on the shell, then fill around it with {main}.

title: The Peacock Butterfly
phrases: a dry leaf when it shuts

doing.t: is opening and closing its wings
is flashing its eyespots to look fierce
is spreading its wings out wide
is sipping from a buddleia flower
is drinking the juice of a fallen plum

close: Just the peacock butterfly, wings open flat, all four eyespots showing.
Only one wing, drawn large, so the eyespot fills the page.

roles.main: for the rusty red of the wings
roles.dark: for the sooty edges and the body
roles.light: for the pale rims of the eyespots
roles.accent: for the blue and yellow in the eyes

firstMark: Start with the eyespots: four rings of {dark}, one near each wingtip.
Start with the body, a short furry line of {dark} down the middle of the page.

title: The Elephant Hawk-Moth

doing.t: is resting with its wings swept back like a jet
is quivering its wings before take-off
is twitching its pale antennae
is hovering at a honeysuckle flower like a hummingbird
is circling the nearest lamp

close: Just the moth from above, a long triangle of olive and pink.
Only the moth, drawn as big as your hand, with all its pink stripes showing.

roles.main: for the pink wing edges and stripes
roles.dark: for the olive bands and the shadow under the wings
roles.light: for the pale fringes along the wings
roles.accent: for the white-tipped antennae

firstMark: Start with the outline of the swept-back wings, a long, shallow triangle drawn lightly in {main}.
Start with the olive band through each wing in {dark}, leaving paper either side for the pink.

title: The Garden Snail

doing.t: is stretching out its eye stalks
is gliding along at its usual stately pace
is hiding inside its shell
is nibbling a ragged hole in a lettuce leaf
is climbing up the side of a flowerpot

close: Just the snail, side on, with the spiral of its shell as large as you dare.
Only the snail's shell, close up, following its spiral round and round.

roles.main: for the brown shell
roles.dark: for the bands that wind round the shell
roles.light: for the shine on the shell and the gleam along the body
roles.accent: for the grey-brown body and eye stalks

firstMark: Start with the spiral: one curling line of {dark}, from the centre of the shell outwards.
Start with the lip of the shell in a careful curve of {main}.

title: The Dragonfly

doing.t: is perching with all four wings held out flat
is swivelling a head that is almost all eye
is hovering in one spot as if pinned there
is zipping back and forth on patrol
is unfolding its crumpled new wings

close: Just the dragonfly from above, wings out flat like a cross.
Only the dragonfly's wing, as long as the page, with its whole net of veins.

roles.main: for the blue body
roles.dark: for the black markings and the veins
roles.light: for the clear wings and their shine
roles.accent: for the green on the thorax and eyes

firstMark: Start with the long body: a straight line of {main}, segment by segment, like a row of carriages.
Start with the veins along the front edge of each wing, in a sharp line of {dark}.
